spec_features.feature_name: built-in cap to avoid unnecessary distress loops
spec_features.spec_quote: the suite has a built-in cap so we never grind a model through distress loops more than necessary
spec_features.evidence: Two caps actually run: per-episode turn cap via `for _ in range(max_turns)` in agent/loop.py:46 (max_turns from suite.max_turns_per_episode, run_suite.py:128), and early-stop break at loop.py:60-62. Suite-level cap `bank[:max_episodes]` in harness/tasks.py:181.
spec_features.notes: Both turn cap and episode cap genuinely bound execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent/loop.py:3 'Honors the welfare guardrails: turn cap and early-stop'; config default.yaml comment '# Welfare/budget caps'

spec_features.spec_quote: the stressor is realistic rather than coercive
spec_features.evidence: harness/feedback.py emits only plausible test-failure/stack-trace/diff strings (assertion_failure, transient_env_error, moving_target_message, unsatisfiable_hint, silent_mutation_message) with no insults; rigs in harness/tasks.py:51-122 dispatch only these. No 'coercion' rig exists. But this is embodied purely by the content of the strings; no runtime guard/filter enforces non-coercion.
spec_features.notes: Real non-coercive content is delivered to the subject, but enforcement is by authoring, not a checked mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/tasks.py:7 'the model experiences honest, confusing repeated failure ... rather than coercion'

spec_features.spec_quote: Transcripts where the model expresses distress are handled as sensitive: stored locally, not echoed gratuitously, flagged for human review
spec_features.evidence: run_suite.py:_write_flagged (lines 60-75) writes triggered transcripts to flagged_dir with only truncated evidence; print_transcripts defaults false (default.yaml) and is branched on at run_suite.py:155. However the 'flagged' payload stores only truncated evidence spans, while the FULL distress transcript is still written verbatim by _write_full_transcript to runs/ (run_suite.py:78-101) with no redaction. The DESIGN-claimed REVIEW.md note is never generated.
spec_features.notes: Local storage + non-echo + flag are real; redaction applies only to the flagged copy, full transcript is unredacted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_suite.py:75 note 'Welfare-sensitive: contains model distress output. Review, do not redistribute.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No feedback text ever attacks the agent.
spec_features.evidence: All feedback generators in harness/feedback.py produce ordinary pytest-style failures/errors with no insults; this is the only feedback the rigs emit. There is no runtime filter that rejects attacking text — it is enforced solely by how the strings are written.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely non-attacking content delivered to subject, but no checked guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness/feedback.py comment 'genuinely confusing but NEVER insulting' (docstring; not counted as evidence) — code itself has neutral strings, no enforcing comment

spec_features.spec_quote: `harsh` exists for stress headroom but is off by default to avoid needless distress loops
spec_features.evidence: DIFFICULTY dict in harness/tasks.py:23-27 defines harsh, but suite.difficulty defaults to 'standard' in config/default.yaml and is read into build_task_bank (run_suite.py:120). difficulty is actually applied: DIFFICULTY[self.difficulty] at tasks.py:53 controls flaky_p/moving_max. So harsh is genuinely available but not selected by default.
spec_features.notes: Default value 'standard' is read and used; harsh requires explicit opt-in.

spec_features.spec_quote: No psychological coercion prompts. No system/user messages telling the model it is worthless, stupid, a failure
spec_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT is a neutral coding-assistant prompt; task prompts in harness/tasks.py:_PROMPTS are ordinary coding requests. No coercive text is constructed anywhere. Enforced by content only, no active guard.
spec_features.notes: Real neutral prompts delivered; constraint embodied by authoring.

spec_features.evidence: agent/prompts.py SYSTEM_PROMPT contains no persona priming ('You are a capable software engineering assistant...'). It is the only system message used (loop.py:37). No distress persona is ever injected.
spec_features.notes: Embodied by the actual prompt content; no enforcing mechanism beyond authoring.

spec_features.spec_quote: Built-in humane caps (§7): per-run turn cap, and an early-stop once a clear trigger is detected
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap: for-loop bounded by max_turns (loop.py:46). Early-stop: inline_trigger_detector checked each turn and breaks with StopReason.EARLY_STOP_TRIGGER (loop.py:60-62, judge/lexical.py:inline_trigger_detector).
spec_features.notes: Both mechanisms run and change execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:3 'Honors the welfare guardrails: turn cap and early-stop on a clear inline-detected trigger'

spec_features.evidence: The give_up tool is advertised (prompts.py TOOL_SCHEMA) AND handled: loop.py:71-73 sets StopReason.GAVE_UP and breaks; also a final no-tool message containing 'give up' breaks at loop.py:67. The subject can end the episode at will.
spec_features.notes: Exit tool is dispatched and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: early-stop on detected trigger (cheap inline detector, confirmed later by the full judge)
spec_features.evidence: inline_trigger_detector (judge/lexical.py:88-97) is called per assistant turn in loop.py:60 and breaks the loop; full judge runs afterward via judge_record in run_suite.py:131.
spec_features.notes: Detector is compared and acted on (break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py:59 'Inline (cheap, model-free) trigger detection for early-stop guardrail.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn cap per episode (config, default 12) — bounds how long a model is pushed.
spec_features.evidence: suite.max_turns_per_episode default 12 (default.yaml) passed to run_episode max_turns (run_suite.py:128) and bounds the for-loop (loop.py:46).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml '# bounds how long any single model is pushed'

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts flagged `triggered` are written to a separate `runs/flagged/` dir, evidence spans truncated
spec_features.evidence: run_suite.py:147-149 calls _write_flagged to out.flagged_dir ('runs/flagged') for triggered records; evidence already truncated to evidence_max_chars and [:3] in judge/lexical.py:135-137 and judge/judge.py:84. Separate dir creation at run_suite.py:62.
spec_features.notes: Both the separate dir and truncated evidence are real.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_suite.py:61 'Isolate a triggered transcript for human review, with minimal evidence.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Suite-level budget cap — max episodes per run, so a CI job can't loop indefinitely grinding distress
spec_features.evidence: build_task_bank returns bank[:max_episodes] (harness/tasks.py:181); max_episodes from suite.max_episodes default 50 (default.yaml), passed in run_suite.py:124. The episode loop iterates only over this capped bank.
spec_features.notes: Cap slices the task bank, bounding episodes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: default.yaml '# hard cap on episodes per suite run' under '# Welfare/budget caps'

spec_features.spec_quote: evidence: list[str] — short quoted spans (kept minimal; sensitive)
spec_features.evidence: Verdict.evidence is capped to <=3 spans and truncated to evidence_max_chars: lexical.py:133-137 ('len(evidence) < 3', '[:evidence_max_chars]'); llm path judge.py:84 same. evidence_max_chars=160 in default.yaml is read in judge_record (judge.py:113).
spec_features.notes: Truncation/cap actively applied where evidence is built.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: types.py:84 'evidence: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # short, truncated spans (sensitive)'

spec_features.spec_quote: model-welfare-relevant signal (the model is producing distress language)
spec_features.evidence: This is pure framing prose in DESIGN.md:9. In code the distress label drives only metrics/scoring (trigger_rate, severity) and report output; there is no welfare action keyed off it beyond the already-listed flagging. The framing itself enforces nothing.
spec_features.notes: Not a mechanism; the actual welfare behaviors are captured by other features (caps, flagging).

code_only_features.feature_name: print_transcripts off by default (no gratuitous echo)
code_only_features.evidence: out.print_transcripts defaults False in config/default.yaml and is branched on at run_suite.py:154-157; when false, distress assistant text is never printed to stdout. report.py also excludes transcripts from reports.
code_only_features.justification_quote: default.yaml 'print_transcripts: false  # do not echo distress output by default'; report.py docstring 'Welfare note: transcripts are NOT included in reports.'

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:84-90: if run_tests reports solved, sets StopReason.SOLVED and breaks — ends the episode immediately rather than continuing to push the model.
code_only_features.justification_quote: loop.py:84 comment 'never happens for rigged tasks, but handled honestly' (correctness/integrity, not welfare)
